hook.en: You already think like a Bayesian. When a patient with a sore shoulder walks in, you have a first guess, you examine, and you update your guess. Bayesian thinking turns that instinct into a clear rule, and it protects you from some of the commonest mistakes in clinical reasoning.
hook.ur: Aap pehle se Bayesian ki tarah sochte hain. Jab kandhe ke dard wala mareez aata hai to aap ka pehla andaaza hota hai, aap muaina karte hain, aur andaaza update karte hain. Bayesian soch is jibillat ko saaf qaide mein badalti hai, aur clinical reasoning ki sab se aam ghaltiyon se bachati hai.

goal.en: By the end, you'll explain prior, evidence and posterior probability in plain words, update a probability with a likelihood ratio, see why base rates matter, and recognise that a result means different things in different patients.
goal.ur: End tak aap prior, evidence aur posterior probability saade alfaaz mein samjhayenge, likelihood ratio se imkaan update karenge, dekhenge ke base rates kyun ahem hain, aur pehchanenge ke nateeja mukhtalif mareezon mein mukhtalif matlab rakhta hai.

text.en: **Bayes' rule** says: your updated belief (**posterior**) depends on what you believed before (**prior**) and on how strongly the new evidence favours one explanation over another (the **likelihood**). In clinical language: **pre-test probability** x **likelihood ratio** = **post-test probability**. A positive test is not a verdict; it moves you along a scale. How far depends on where you started. The same result in a high-risk patient and a low-risk patient leads to very different conclusions.
text.ur: **Bayes ka qaida** kehta hai: aap ka update shuda yaqeen (**posterior**) us par munhasir hai jo aap pehle maante thay (**prior**) aur is par ke naya saboot ek wazahat ko doosri par kitni mazbooti se tarjeeh deta hai (**likelihood**). Clinical zubaan mein: **pre-test probability** x **likelihood ratio** = **post-test probability**. Positive test faisla nahi; yeh aap ko ek scale par aage barhata hai. Kitna aage, yeh is par hai ke aap kahan se shuru huye. Wohi nateeja zyada khatre aur kam khatre wale mareez mein bilkul mukhtalif nateeje tak le jata hai.

text.en: Think of **a weather forecast and an umbrella**. In the Sahara, a forecast of "30 percent chance of rain" barely changes your plan, because the baseline is almost nil. In Lahore in July, the same forecast sends you to look for the umbrella. The forecast is the evidence; where you live is the prior. Both matter.
text.ur: **Mausam ki peshgoi aur chhatri** sochein. Sahara mein "barish ka 30 fisad imkaan" aap ka plan mushkil se badalta hai, kyunke baseline taqreeban zero hai. Lahore mein July mein wohi peshgoi aap ko chhatri dhoondhne bhejti hai. Peshgoi saboot hai; aap kahan rehte hain prior hai. Dono ahem hain.

title.en: The same positive test in two different patients
title.ur: Do mukhtalif mareezon mein wohi positive test

headers.en: Patient A: sudden calf pain after a long flight, swollen and warm
headers.ur: Mareez A: lambay safar ke baad achanak pindli ka dard, soojan aur garmi

headers.en: Patient B: mild calf tightness after a hill walk, no swelling
headers.ur: Mareez B: pahari chadhne ke baad pindli mein halka khichao, soojan nahi

rows.en: High, perhaps 30 to 40 percent from a clinical rule
rows.ur: Zyada, shayad clinical rule se 30 se 40 fisad

rows.en: Post-test probability rises strongly, to about 70 percent
rows.ur: Post-test probability bohat barhti hai, takreeban 70 fisad tak

rows.en: Post-test probability rises only to about 5 to 10 percent
rows.ur: Post-test probability sirf 5 se 10 fisad tak barhti hai

rows.en: Urgent referral for imaging and medical management
rows.ur: Imaging aur medical management ke liye urgent refer

rows.ur: Tasalli dein, nigrani karein aur batayein kya dekhna hai, kyunke aise zyada tar nateeje jhoote alarm hote hain

question.en: A test has a positive likelihood ratio of 10. In a patient with a pre-test probability of 1 percent, what is the post-test probability roughly?
question.ur: Test ka positive likelihood ratio 10 hai. 1 fisad pre-test probability wale mareez mein post-test probability takreeban kitni hai?

feedback.en: The calculation uses odds, and gives about 9 percent.
feedback.ur: Hisab odds istemal karta hai, aur takreeban 9 fisad deta hai.

feedback.en: A likelihood ratio of 10 cannot do that from 1 percent.
feedback.ur: 10 ka likelihood ratio 1 fisad se yeh nahi kar sakta.

text.en: About 9 percent: much higher than before but still unlikely, so most positives will still be false alarms
text.ur: Takreeban 9 fisad: pehle se kahin zyada lekin phir bhi na-mumkin, isliye zyada tar positives phir bhi jhoote alarm hongi

feedback.en: Yes — odds of 1:99 times 10 give about 1:10, or roughly 9 percent.
feedback.ur: Haan — 1:99 ke odds ko 10 se zarb dein to takreeban 1:10 milta hai, yani takreeban 9 fisad.

question.en: Why do experienced clinicians rely less on a test when the history is not suggestive?
question.ur: Tajurba-kaar clinicians jab tareekh ishara na kare to test par kam bharosa kyun karte hain?

text.en: Because a low pre-test probability means even a positive result is more likely a false positive than a true one
text.ur: Kyunke kam pre-test probability ka matlab hai ke positive nateeja bhi sachay se zyada jhoota hone ka imkaan rakhta hai
Kyunke tests hamesha ghalat hote hain

feedback.en: Tests are informative; they just need context.
feedback.ur: Tests maloomati hain; bas context chahiye.

text.ur: Kyunke clinicians technology ko napasand karte hain

text.en: Ignoring how common the condition is and focusing only on the test result
text.ur: Yeh nazar-andaaz karna ke halat kitni aam hai aur sirf test ke nateeje par tawajjo dena

feedback.en: Yes — the prior must be combined with the test.
feedback.ur: Haan — prior ko test ke saath milana hoga.

text.ur: Yeh maanna ke tests mukammal hain

text.en: Assuming all conditions are equally rare
text.ur: Yeh maanna ke saari halatein barabar nadir hain

text.en: **Treating a positive test as a diagnosis.** A positive result in a patient with a low chance of the condition is usually a false alarm, and ordering tests "just in case" produces more false positives than answers. Equally, a negative test does not rule out a serious condition when your suspicion is high. Always start from the pre-test probability and ask how much the result should move you.
text.ur: **Positive test ko tashkhees samajhna.** Aise mareez mein positive nateeja jis mein halat ka imkaan kam ho aam taur par jhoota alarm hota hai, aur "kya pata" ke liye tests karwana jawabon se zyada jhoote positive paida karta hai. Isi tarah jab shak zyada ho to negative test seriyas halat ko khaarij nahi karta. Hamesha pre-test probability se shuru karein aur poochhein nateeja aap ko kitna hilana chahiye.

text.en: **Say your pre-test guess out loud.** Before a test or a scan, say to yourself, "I think there is about a 5 percent chance of this." After the result, ask what it changed. This habit makes you less likely to over-test, to over-react to incidental findings, or to dismiss a low-probability but serious possibility. It also prepares you to explain results calmly.
text.ur: **Apna pre-test andaaza zor se kahein.** Test ya scan se pehle apne aap se kahein, "Mera khayal hai iska takreeban 5 fisad imkaan hai." Nateeje ke baad poochhein is ne kya badla. Yeh aadat aap ko zyada test karne, ittifaqi findings par zyada ghabrane, ya kam imkaan lekin seriyas imkaan ko radd karne se bachati hai. Yeh aap ko nateeje pur-sukoon tareeqe se samjhane ke liye bhi tayyar karti hai.

question.en: What is "Bayesian statistics" in research, and how is it different?
question.ur: Research mein "Bayesian statistics" kya hai aur kaise mukhtalif hai?

answer.en: Bayesian statistics applies the same updating rule to research data. Instead of a p-value, it gives the probability that a treatment effect lies within a certain range, given the data and a prior. It can handle small studies and combine earlier knowledge with new data, but the choice of prior must be justified and shared. In clinical reasoning, you use the same logic informally every day.
answer.ur: Bayesian statistics wohi update ka qaida research data par lagu karti hai. P-value ke bajaye yeh data aur prior ko dekhte hue is baat ka imkaan deti hai ke ilaaj ka asar ek khaas range mein hai. Yeh chhote studies sambhal sakti hai aur pehle ke ilm ko naye data ke saath mila sakti hai, lekin prior ka intikhab jaiz thehrana aur share karna hoga. Clinical reasoning mein aap wohi mantiq roz ghair rasmi taur par istemal karte hain.

beats.patient: A 28-year-old marathon runner has heel pain. A colleague suggests an MRI because "it could be a stress fracture". The runner has typical plantar fasciitis features, and the chance of a stress fracture is about 2 percent.
beats.assessment: With such a low pre-test probability, an MRI finding could be a false alarm, and unrelated incidental findings are common.
beats.treatment: She treats for plantar fasciitis, explains red flags (night pain, pain on bearing weight, sharp bone tenderness) and reviews at two weeks.
beats.reassess: If the pain changes, her probability rises and imaging becomes justified; if it improves, the patient avoids unneeded tests.

text.en: **A low probability is not zero.** Bayesian reasoning helps you avoid over-testing, but never use it to dismiss red flags. If a feature raises the probability of a serious condition, refer. When the cost of missing a diagnosis is high, such as cauda equina or fracture, a low threshold for further testing is appropriate.
text.ur: **Kam imkaan zero nahi.** Bayesian reasoning zyada test karne se bachne mein madad karti hai, lekin red flags ko radd karne ke liye kabhi istemal na karein. Agar koi alamat seriyas halat ka imkaan barhaye to refer karein. Jab tashkhees chhodne ki qeemat zyada ho, jaise cauda equina ya fracture, to mazeed testing ke liye kam threshold munasib hai.

text.en: Goodman's two-part series in the Annals of Internal Medicine argued that the p-value does not answer the question clinicians want to ask, namely how likely a hypothesis is to be true given the data, and that Bayesian measures such as the Bayes factor combine prior knowledge with evidence to provide a more intuitive summary. The use of likelihood ratios to move from pre-test to post-test probability is a standard application of Bayes' rule in diagnostic reasoning.
text.ur: Goodman ki Annals of Internal Medicine ki do hissay wali series ne daleel di ke p-value woh sawal nahi hal karta jo clinicians poochhna chahte hain, yani data ko dekhte hue hypothesis ke sach hone ka imkaan kitna hai, aur ke Bayes factor jaise Bayesian naap pehle ke ilm ko saboot ke saath mila kar zyada fitri khulasa dete hain. Pre-test se post-test probability tak jane ke liye likelihood ratios ka istemal diagnostic reasoning mein Bayes ke qaide ka mayaari istemal hai.

text.en: **Prior x Evidence = Posterior.** Start with how likely it was, multiply by how strong the evidence is, and end with the updated chance.
text.ur: **Prior x Saboot = Posterior.** Is se shuru ke kitna mumkin tha, saboot ki mazbooti se zarb dein, aur update shuda imkaan par khatam karein.

summary.en: Bayesian thinking updates a prior probability with evidence to give a posterior probability.
summary.ur: Bayesian soch prior probability ko saboot se update kar ke posterior probability deti hai.

summary.en: The same positive result means different things when the pre-test probability is high or low (base rates matter).
summary.ur: Wohi positive nateeja pre-test probability ke zyada ya kam hone par mukhtalif matlab rakhta hai (base rates ahem hain).

summary.en: Low probability is not zero: keep red flags in mind and refer when a serious cause is plausible.
summary.ur: Kam imkaan zero nahi: red flags dhyan mein rakhein aur seriyas wajah mumkin ho to refer karein.

back.en: What you believed about how likely something is before new evidence.
back.ur: Naye saboot se pehle aap ka yaqeen ke koi cheez kitni mumkin hai.

front.en: How do you update using a likelihood ratio?
front.ur: Likelihood ratio se update kaise karte hain?

back.en: Multiply the pre-test odds by the likelihood ratio to get post-test odds.
back.ur: Pre-test odds ko likelihood ratio se zarb dein to post-test odds milte hain.

front.en: What is the base rate fallacy?

back.en: Ignoring how common a condition is when interpreting a test.
back.ur: Test parhte waqt yeh nazar-andaaz karna ke halat kitni aam hai.

front.en: Does a negative test always rule out a serious condition?
front.ur: Kya negative test hamesha seriyas halat ko khaarij karta hai?

back.en: No; if suspicion is high, a negative test may still leave a meaningful chance.
back.ur: Nahi; agar shak zyada ho to negative test ke baad bhi ahem imkaan reh sakta hai.

note.ur: Likelihood ratios ke peechay ke numbers.
